name: Question 7
problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1){e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\times ⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ (t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 0 \\ -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,{e}^{2t}⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{((t+1){e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(t+1)^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{({e}^{2t})}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨tet,−et,4⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
tett2+2
b
te2tt2+2t+2
c
1ett2+2
d
ett2+2t+2
e
ett2+2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(tet),ddt(−et),ddt(4)⟩=⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt((t+1)et),ddt(−et),ddt(0)⟩=⟨(t+2)et,−et,0⟩

Now, we compute v×a,||v|| and ||v×a||:

v×a=⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩×⟨(t+2)et,−et,0⟩=ijk(t+1)et−et0(t+2)et−et0= −et0−et0i−(t+1)et0(t+2)et0j+(t+1)et−et(t+2)et−etk=⟨0,0,e2t⟩,||v||=((t+1)et)2+(−et)2+(0)2=(t+1)2e2t+e2t=ett2+2t+2,||v×a||=(0)2+(0)2+(e2t)2=e2t

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get aN=||v×a||||v||=e2tett2+2t+2=ett2+2t+2.
